bottleneck: Beyond small indels, CRISPR double-strand breaks can cause translocations between on- and off-target cut sites, plus large deletions, inversions, duplications, and chromosomal loss. These structural variants represent genotoxicity that standard bulk sequencing can miss entirely, and unintended integration of HDR donor templates adds another failure mode. The FDA's April 2026 guidance specifically flags translocation assessment as required.
current_state: Long-read and single-cell assays are beginning to reveal the true scale of structural damage, but standardized, sensitive detection is not yet routine in development pipelines.

sources.title: The off-target problem the gene editing industry can no longer afford to ignore

title: Editing-induced translocations and chromosomal damage evade detection
why_it_blocks: A therapy that occasionally scrambles chromosomes can seed cancer years later. Until structural genotoxicity is reliably detected and prevented, systemic nuclease therapies carry a latent safety liability that regulators cannot accept.
